title: Choosing speech use cases · Level 3
slo: Identify when speech recognition, speech synthesis, or both fit a workplace need.

exercises.question_text: Which tasks can a voice assistant accept as spoken commands? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Correct. Voice assistants can accept a spoken request to set a reminder.
Correct. Sending messages is a task voice assistants can receive as a spoken command.
Correct. A person can speak a request to search for information.

options.error_type: Confuses spoken input with synthesized output
options.rationale: Reading an article aloud is audio output from written text. It is not a spoken command being received.
options.better_fit: Use this when someone wants to consume written content while driving, exercising, or away from a screen.

feedback.intrinsic: The person could issue a command, but the article would not be spoken aloud.
feedback.instructional: Speech recognition receives spoken commands; speech synthesis produces spoken articles.

exercises.explanation: Correct. A voice assistant can receive spoken requests to set reminders, send messages, and search.

exercises.question_text: Where can a clinician dictate patient notes with speech recognition?

options.rationale: Correct. Clinical professionals can dictate patient notes directly into electronic health records.

options.error_type: Confuses clinical dictation with voice-agent output
options.rationale: A phone response speaks information aloud. Dictation captures a clinician’s spoken notes as written documentation.
options.better_fit: Use this when a phone channel needs to answer callers aloud.

feedback.intrinsic: The patient note would not be entered where care records are kept.
feedback.instructional: Clinical dictation uses recognition to place spoken notes into electronic health records.

options.error_type: Confuses healthcare documentation with spoken alerts
options.rationale: Navigation applications announce directions. They are not where clinicians document patient care.
options.better_fit: Use this when spoken navigation instructions are needed.

feedback.intrinsic: Important care details would not be captured in the patient record.
feedback.instructional: Recognition supports clinical notes and treatment-plan updates in electronic health records.

options.rationale: A game character script belongs to media creation. It does not store clinical documentation.
options.better_fit: Use this when creating spoken character voices for a game.

feedback.intrinsic: The clinician’s notes would not be available in the care record.
feedback.instructional: For patient documentation, dictate into an electronic health record.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Dictating into electronic health records captures care details while reducing typing.

exercises.question_text: Speech synthesis can read articles aloud for a person with dyslexia.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The person may be left without the useful audio alternative to reading.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Synthesis can read articles and documents aloud for people with reading disabilities or visual impairments.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Spoken articles provide an alternative way to consume written content for people with dyslexia.

exercises.question_text: What can speech synthesis create for a game?

options.rationale: Correct. Creators can use synthesis to generate character voices for games and interactive experiences.

options.error_type: Confuses media synthesis with call recognition
options.rationale: A call record is written text produced from spoken customer calls. A character voice is generated audio.
options.better_fit: Use this in a service center that needs searchable records from customer calls.

feedback.intrinsic: The game would have no generated character voice.
feedback.instructional: Recognition creates written call records; synthesis creates spoken media.

options.rationale: Live captions are written output from ongoing speech. A game character voice is spoken audio output.
options.better_fit: Use this to make a live meeting accessible to people who are deaf or hard of hearing.

feedback.intrinsic: Players would not hear the character’s generated voice.
feedback.instructional: Captions use recognition. Character voices use synthesis.

options.error_type: Confuses generated audio with clinical dictation
options.rationale: A dictated patient note is clinical documentation created from spoken input. It is not an audio asset for a game.
options.better_fit: Use this when clinicians need to capture patient notes in electronic health records.

feedback.intrinsic: The game’s character would remain without a voice.
feedback.instructional: Synthesis creates audio for media; recognition supports dictated notes.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Speech synthesis can create character voices for games and interactive experiences.

exercises.question_text: Which information can speech synthesis announce? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Correct. Synthesis can announce reminders as spoken audio.
Correct. Spoken status updates can reach people who cannot look at a screen.
Correct. Mapping and GPS applications can announce navigation instructions.

options.error_type: Confuses spoken alerts with recognition analysis
options.rationale: Caller sentiment is something analyzed from spoken calls. It is not an alert that synthesis announces.
options.better_fit: Use this when analyzing customer calls for sentiment and common issues.

feedback.intrinsic: Important alerts could go unheard while attention is on another task.
feedback.instructional: Synthesis announces information; recognition can analyze what callers say.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Synthesis can announce reminders, updates, and directions when visual attention is unavailable.

exercises.question_text: A combined voice experience uses recognition for spoken input and synthesis for spoken output.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The interaction would be missing either the spoken request or the spoken response.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Two-way voice experiences combine recognition for input with synthesis for output.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Recognition handles what the person says, and synthesis provides the spoken reply or confirmation.

exercises.question_text: Which results can meeting transcription create? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Correct. Recognition can create written meeting notes that people can search.
Correct. Transcribed conversations can support action-item lists for follow-up.
Correct. Recognition can provide captions while people are speaking.
Navigation directions are spoken audio output. Meeting transcription produces written notes, lists, or captions.
options.better_fit: Use this when drivers need spoken directions without visual attention.

feedback.intrinsic: Participants would not receive written notes or captions from the meeting.
feedback.instructional: Recognition turns meeting speech into text; synthesis can announce navigation directions.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Recognition can make meeting content searchable, actionable, and accessible through captions.

exercises.question_text: Reconstruct the statement from the pieces.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The accessibility benefit is hard to understand in the mixed-up sentence.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Name synthesis, then its spoken action, then the people it supports.

exercises.correct_answer: Speech synthesis reads web content aloud for people with visual impairments
exercises.explanation: The sentence states how written web content becomes accessible as spoken audio. The final phrase identifies who benefits from that alternative.

exercises.question_text: In a combined voice experience, speech recognition handles spoken ___.

parts.text: In a combined voice experience, speech recognition handles spoken

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The person’s spoken request would not be understood as the start of the interaction.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Output, narration, and alerts are spoken results. Recognition handles spoken input.

exercises.explanation: Recognition listens to a person’s words and converts them to text, so it handles the input side of a two-way voice interaction. Synthesis handles the spoken output side.

exercises.question_text: Arrange the parts to form the correct statement.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The workplace need for hands-free control is unclear.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Put the assistant first, then what it accepts, then the screen-limited situation.

exercises.correct_answer: Voice assistants accept spoken commands when screens are impractical
exercises.explanation: The sentence first names the capability, then its action, and finally the situation where hands-free use helps. Voice assistants are useful when screens are impractical.

exercises.question_text: Speech recognition can provide real-time ___ for people who are deaf or hard of hearing.

parts.text: for people who are deaf or hard of hearing.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A participant could miss spoken parts of the conversation.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Voiceovers, directions, and podcast drafts are audio outputs. Recognition provides live captions from speech.

exercises.explanation: Recognition converts current spoken content into written captions. This makes live conversations more accessible to people who are deaf or hard of hearing.

exercises.question_text: What can synthesized narration provide in language learning?

options.rationale: Correct. Educational platforms can use synthesized speech to provide pronunciation examples.

options.error_type: Confuses learning audio with call transcription
options.rationale: Call records are written transcriptions of spoken customer calls. Pronunciation examples are audio created for learners.
options.better_fit: Use this in service centers that need searchable customer-call documentation.

feedback.intrinsic: Learners would not hear how the words are pronounced.
feedback.instructional: Synthesis creates spoken pronunciation examples; recognition creates written call records.

options.error_type: Confuses narrated learning with service recognition
options.rationale: Caller routing uses spoken requests to direct a call. It does not provide audio for language learning.
options.better_fit: Use this when customer calls need to reach the appropriate department.

feedback.intrinsic: Learners would receive no pronunciation support.
feedback.instructional: For language practice, synthesis can speak examples aloud.

options.error_type: Confuses audio output with clinical speech input
options.rationale: Patient-note dictation converts a clinician’s spoken words into written documentation. It is not narrated learning content.
options.better_fit: Use this when clinical professionals need to enter notes into electronic health records.

feedback.intrinsic: The course would not provide a spoken pronunciation model.
feedback.instructional: Pronunciation examples are synthesized audio, while dictation uses recognition.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Synthesized narration can give learners clear pronunciation examples.
